belief: I'm turning into my own parents.
origins: Many of us hear our parent’s words come out of our own mouths and feel a chill. If we grew up with anger, coldness, addiction, or control, we may fear that we are destined to repeat it. The fear can be so strong that it makes us anxious, hypervigilant, or afraid to be close to our children.
teaches: Paul says, “Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!” God promises, “I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.” The fruit of the Spirit is “love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.” Paul also says, “I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.” Patterns can pass down, but they are not destiny. Noticing the pattern is the first step in breaking it.
self_statements: I am becoming exactly what I swore I would not.
My children will end up like me.
I never had a good model.
I will repeat the same cycle.
errors: Predicting that I will repeat the past.
Believing I am either totally different or the same.
Feeling afraid and concluding that it is inevitable.
questions: In what specific ways do I notice I am like my parent, and in what ways am I different?
What good qualities did I also receive from them?
What triggers my reactions, and what can I do differently in that moment?
What does Scripture say about a new heart?
Who can help me learn new ways to parent?
What small change can I make today?
truth: I am not doomed to repeat my parents’ patterns. In Christ I am a new creation, and God gives me a new heart and His Spirit. I can notice old reactions, pause, repair, and practice new ones.
hw_truths: I am a new creation in Christ.
God gives me a new heart.
The Spirit produces patience and gentleness in me.
log: Each week, write one moment you noticed an old reaction and how you responded differently or repaired.
actions: Write ways your parenting is already different from theirs.
Decide on a phrase or action to use when you are triggered.
Read a book, take a class, or see a counselor on parenting.
When you slip, apologize and try again.
prayer: Lord, I fear repeating what I grew up with. Make me new. Give me a heart that is gentle and patient, and teach me ways of loving my children that I never saw. Amen.
hw_questions: How am I like my parent?
What will I do in the moment?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I am a new creation in Christ, not a copy of my parents.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I'm turning into my own parents.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
